reasoning_traces.think:
The dynamic Bradley-Terry model extends the classic Bradley-Terry framework to time-varying contexts using kernel smoothing. At each time point t, the raw pairwise comparison matrix X_ij(t) is replaced by a smoothed version X̃_ij(t) obtained through convolution with a Gaussian kernel W_h(t, t_m). This smoothing operation allows for more stable estimation even when individual time slices contain sparse data. The resulting smoothed data is then used to fit a static Bradley-Terry model, yielding time-dependent team strengths β_i(t). The key insight is that smoothing reduces variance in estimates while preserving the essential structure of the original model. The theoretical guarantees provided by oracle bounds ensure that these estimates remain close to the optimal solution under idealized conditions. These bounds depend on the kernel bandwidth h, which is selected via LOOCV to balance bias and variance. The existence and uniqueness of solutions are guaranteed by a strong connectivity condition on the smoothed graph, ensuring that every group of teams can be compared indirectly through transitivity. This makes the model robust to missing data and suitable for applications like sports rankings where teams may not play each other directly.
